text: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "Here we are—we are your own flesh and blood.

"Even before now, while Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them home. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"

versions.text: Even before now, while Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought it home. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"
versions.explanation: Two small points: the speech begun in verse 1 continues here, so an opening quotation mark is needed for clarity in oral reading; and referring to Israel as "it" clashes with the plural sense used elsewhere ("my people Israel"), so "them" reads more naturally.

text: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

The king and his men marched on Jerusalem against the Jebusites who lived there. They said to David, "You will never get in here. Even the blind and the lame could drive you off"—meaning, "David will never get in here."
But David captured the stronghold of Zion—that is, the City of David.

That day David said, "Whoever attacks the Jebusites must go up through the water shaft to reach the lame and the blind, those whom David hates." That is why they say, "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house."
David took up residence in the stronghold and called it the City of David, and he built up the area around it, from the Millo inward.
And David went on and grew greater and greater, for the LORD God of hosts was with him.

versions.text: And David grew stronger and stronger, for the LORD God of hosts was with him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb גדל means to become great (in stature, honor, and power), not specifically "strong" (which would be חזק). "Greater and greater" better captures the idiom of increasing greatness.

text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.
Then David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
After he came from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all came up to search for him; and when David heard of it, he went down to the stronghold.
The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
So David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go up, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand."
So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated them there. He said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a bursting flood." That is why he named that place Baal-perazim.
The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.
Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
So David inquired of the LORD, and he answered, "Do not go straight up. Circle around behind them and attack them opposite the balsam trees.
As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly, for then the LORD has gone out ahead of you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
David did as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.
